purpose: Exercise the official MAST API with a bounded TESS time-series metadata request and verify HTTP response, JSON parsing, schema, observation identifiers, and output hash. No light-curve product bytes were downloaded and no model or scientific classification was evaluated.

source.request_format: JSON encoded as form parameter request
source.reference_semantics: Observation/product metadata, not labels or independent astrophysical ground truth.

execution.method: Python standard-library urllib POST; JSON parse

output_artifacts.reason: Raw response was not committed; compact metadata and hash are retained.

facts: MAST returned HTTP 200 and a COMPLETE JSON response for the bounded request.
The response was 2,257 bytes with SHA-256 9c7f145e96b53df393ad61274186bc3788ecd596ee4423b3d4f1daa19080b098.
Five rows were returned with five unique obsid values and five unique obs_id values.
The service reported 1,994,189 rows matching the filters; only the first page of five was requested.
unresolved: This is metadata-only; no TESS time-series files were acquired.
The metadata response does not establish a deterministic order across repeated queries because no explicit server-side sort parameter was tested.
Product-specific time units, flux units, quality flags, processing level, checksums, and licensing still need to be recorded after selecting an exact product.
claims_not_supported: Direct comparability between TESS and ZTF light curves
Resolution of the CPVS membership discrepancy

next_actions: Choose an exact TESS product and bounded observation/target list; retrieve product metadata and product checksum before download.
Test the production MAST adapter and operation journal on a pinned product.
Use a known malformed response to verify failure evidence is persisted.
